newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond spreads hold amid mounting supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond spreads hold amid mounting supply.

text.p: U.S. high-grades corporate bonds closed slightly lower and spreads were mostly unchanged as several new issues piled up in the primary, dealers said.
High-yield bonds endured spotty setbacks in thin trade as investors there held off for new issuances, traders said.
Investment grades spreads were under pressure to widen in general, traders said, but the softness was not widespread. Traders reiterated the market was still cash rich.
"There are some deals getting done, but remember there wasn't a lot to look at before," one trader said. "It was fairly quiet today but the market will withstand the supply."

Because the market has run so far so fast, however, some traders see the market diverging by sector. Areas like Yankees and utlities could use the supply, while the rally in telephone debt could be tapped, one trader said.
Swapping activity comprised much of the business on Monday, according to one big New York shop. Some also reported heavier retail orders at mid-session.
The high-grade primary market featured $300 million in 10-year A1/A-plus rated notes from WMX Technologies, priced to yield 7.04 percent, or 54 basis points over the when-issued 10-year Treasury.
The Merrill Lynch & Co Inc-managed deal was increased in size by $100 million to meet demand, a manager said.

The Bank and finance sector was enlivened by $300 million in issues from PaineWebber Inc and Bear Stearns & Co. PaineWebber's $150 million 12-year non-callable notes were priced as 7-5/8s to yield 7.637 percent, or 112.5 basis points over the when-issued 10-year Treasury. Bear Stearns priced another $150 million 10-year senior notes as 7.25s at par.
Elsewhere, Becton Dickinson issued $100 million A1/A-plus 10-year notes to yield 6.919 percent, or 40 basis points over Treasuries. Goldman Sachs & Co was lead manager on the deal.

New issues were trading unchanged from Monday's close, traders said. Smith Barney Holdings' $200 million 7.125 percent 10-year notes were seen trading at the original issue spread of 68 basis points over the Treasury curve.

In high-yield trade, prices were down 1/8 point on average in the second consecutive day of thin trade, dealers said. More than one trader said investors appeared to be holding off for new issuance later this week.
Uniforet's $100 million 144A 11-1/8 percent debt were quoted at 100-1/2 bid, 101 offer on Tuesday, up from par sale late on Monday, one trader said.
Penn Traffic Co's debt resumed its downward trend. The 8-5/8 percent notes traded within 79 and 81-1/4 and the 10.25 percent notes fell 1/2 point to trade at 86-1/2.
Ralphs Grocery 10.45 percent notes closed at 102-1/4 bid, 102-3/4 offer and the 11 percent notes went out at 101-1/4 bid, 101-5/8 offer -- both issues unchanged.

One new junk issue priced late on Tuesday. Dealers said Outdoor Systems set $250 million 10-year B1/single-B notes at par to yield 9.375 percent. The issue was increased from the $150 million size bandied about early in the session.
CIBC Wood Gundy Securities is lead manager on the deal.

Other junk issues in the pipeline include $225 million in B2/single-B senior subordinated notes of 2006 from Goss Graphic Systems via CS First Boston Corp and $350 million in 144A senior subordinated notes of 2008 from Paging Network Inc via Goldman Sachs & Co.

U.S. Treasuries slipped on Tuesday afternoon following a weaker than expected auction of $10.0 billion U.S. Treasury notes, analysts said. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 7/32 at 99-9/32 to yield 6.81 percent.
